name: Broken Wheel Campground
note: Family-owned campground and country store established 1995, open year round, on Skin Creek Rd about 1.5 mi east of I-79 exit 96 in Lewis County. Operator's own Camping Rates page: campsite with water and 30-amp electric $45/night for 4 people, primitive tent site $25/night, additional persons $2, limited monthly sites; no sewer hookups (dump station on site plus a $20 honey-wagon service for extended stays). Phone reservations only for the W/E sites, taken from March 15 for the season, two-night minimum on May 1-Oct 1 weekends and three on holiday weekends; primitive sites are first-come, not reservable. Store carries groceries, firewood, bait and fishing/hunting supplies; stocked catch-and-release fishing pond (no state licence needed), playground, laundry, wifi. Third-party listings report the 30-amp sites take rigs to about 50 ft with some pull-throughs, which the operator does not state. Official site serves over plain http only - its https certificate chain is broken. RV Life 4*/$$ ~$32/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Operator's own Camping Rates and About pages at brokenwheelcampground.net (fetched live 2026-09-15): $45/night water+30-amp electric campsites and $25/night primitive tent sites, phone reservations opening March 15, open year round, weekend minimum stays -> a real transient drive-in RV campground, not a seasonal or residential park; US Census geocoder matches 2060 Skin Creek Rd to 38.99949,-80.45596 and Esri imagery there shows campers along an interior gravel road beside a store building.

lead.water_body: on-site fishing pond (unnamed); Skin Creek drainage
lead.note: Operator advertises a stocked catch-and-release fishing pond, but Esri imagery is fully leafed-out and no open water is visible anywhere on the property; sites read as scattered under canopy along an interior gravel road set well back from the highway rather than ringed around water.

name: Eagle's Nest Campground
note: Family-owned since 2011 on Patterson Creek Village Pike, about 9 mi from Cumberland MD; open year round. Operator's Camping page: full hook-up sites $50/night ($54 on holiday weekends) and tent camping $20 per adult per night, children 12 and under free. Seasonal packages are sold alongside the nightly sites (weekends-only Thu-Sun $450/month, full-time resident $850/month, May 1-Oct 10 season, a whole row $1800), so expect a mixed transient/seasonal park; cabins and a pavilion are separate products. On-site Fireside Inn restaurant and lounge, camp store (ice, firewood, beer, propane), live music Fridays and karaoke Thursdays, playground and yard games, creek swimming and fishing, weekend community float trips. Reservations and late check-in by phone - there is no online booking. RV Life counts 80 sites; the operator does not publish a site count or a max RV length. Note the operator's own warning that GPS mis-routes to the address - they direct drivers to Patterson Creek Village Pike off WV-28. RV Life 4*/$$ ~$40/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Operator's own Camping, About and Contact pages at eaglesnestcampgroundwv.com (copyright 2026, fetched 2026-09-15): full hook-up RV sites at a published $50/night nightly rate, open year round, office hours and phone; Good Sam listing corroborates 'from $50/night' -> real nightly-bookable RV campground. Esri imagery shows three long rows of RVs on open grass pads with interior gravel lanes and a restaurant building.

lead.note: Operator advertises swimming and fishing in Patterson Creek and 'permanent waterfront lodging'; on Esri imagery the creek runs along the campground's east/southeast edge and the easternmost row of sites sits roughly 30-60 m from it behind a wooded screen, while the two western rows are 100 m or more back in open field.

name: Bradley Campground
skip_reason: Not a campground - a handful of monthly RV hookups on a residential street. RV Life reports 4 sites; the address 6217 Robert C Byrd Dr sits immediately next to Bradley Service Center auto repair at 6215, and Esri imagery shows houses with an occasional RV parked in a yard - no camping loop, pads, restrooms or office (the rows of RVs visible nearby are a dealer/storage lot across the highway). There is no operator website or phone. The only listing is a Hipcamp stub flagged 'Coming soon to Hipcamp' and 'out of stock' (never bookable), whose AI-written blurb says the place 'requires monthly cash payments' and sells proximity to a middle-school bus stop; the identical text is mirrored on pinecliffresort.net, the known campground content farm. Fails inclusion as residential/long-term RV parking with no live web presence.

name: Gheny Nook Campground
note: RV campground in a hollow off WV-92 at mile marker 12.3, 12 mi north of White Sulphur Springs in Greenbrier County; previously T & K Campground and End of the Trail Campground, bought in March 2018 by Bedford McClintic and renamed. Operator's own rates page (archived 2021, site still live August 2025): water / 30-amp electric / sewer sites $35 per night or $200 per week, one premium 50-amp full-hookup site $38 per night or $220 per week, plus limited long-term 'Gheny Nook RV Club' one-year leases; dump station on site, sewer at only a limited number of sites, and the water carries some iron. Reservations by phone call only, no attendant on site, and effectively no cell service - it is inside the National Radio Quiet Zone. CAVEAT: the official domain ghenynook.com changed hands in June 2026 and now 301-redirects to an unrelated pharmacy-spam site, so current operation rests on the operator's Facebook page, the Greenbrier County CVB listing and RV Life's 7 reviews rather than a live site or booking channel - call before relying on it. Esri imagery shows roughly 100 travel trailers along two gravel lanes down the hollow, so expect a long-stay-heavy park with full-time residents present (as Campendium and Roadtrippers both note); RV Life counts 10 sites and tourism listings claim 'over 200 sites', neither confirmed by the operator. Pads are grass/gravel off a gravel lane, reachable by any normal vehicle. RV Life 4*/$$ ~$37/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Operator's own About/Rates page at ghenynook.com via Wayback (2021-09-05 capture; domain still served the same site in Aug 2025): W/E/S 30-amp sites $35/night or $200/week, 50-amp premium $38/night, phone reservations, long-term explicitly 'limited availability' -> a genuinely nightly-priced drive-in RV campground rather than a lease-only park. Esri imagery confirms ~100 travel-trailer pads on two gravel lanes; US Census geocoder matches 12322 Pocahontas Trl to 37.93790,-80.16949, the entrance on WV-92 about 260 m north of the pinned loop.

lead.water_body: unnamed creek in the hollow; on-site fishing ponds per the Greenbrier County CVB listing
lead.note: The CVB listing mentions a 'fresh mountain creek' and fishing ponds; on Esri imagery a wooded drainage runs between the two camping lanes down the hollow and no open water is visible at pad level, so any pond is small and under canopy.

name: Ruby Lake Campground
skip_reason: Residential mobile-home park. It is registered on MHVillage and MobileHomeParkStore as 'Ruby Lake Mobile Home Park', an all-ages community, and Allstays carries it as 'Ruby Lake Campground Mhp' describing 'a small campground located in the middle of a mobile home park'. Esri imagery at the Census-matched address (4 Ruby Lake, 38.89358,-81.67198) shows about 28 permanent single-wide mobile homes on individual lots with driveways and parked cars ringing the small pond - no transient RV pads, no pull-through loop, no picnic-table sites. There is also no operator website and no bookable listing: every source says cash only, first come first served, phone 304-273-3427 - so it fails the live-web-presence test as well as the residential/mobile-home-park exclusion.

name: Prickett's Creek Campground
skip_reason: No evidence it currently operates, and what description exists is long-term. There is no operator website and no bookable listing anywhere: the RVParkStore/RVPark entry was posted 2011-07-05 and never updated, the RoverPass listing is unclaimed and its 'description' is actually text about Prickett's Fort State Park, and ParkAdvisor carries 1.0 stars from 3 reviews reporting the phone 304-363-1910 out of service and the directions wrong. Aggregators place it at three mutually exclusive locations up to 5 km apart - 106 Overfort Ln near Prickett's Fort (39.51451,-80.09559), 955-967 Grafton Rd (39.47620,-80.15206) and 1102 Eastwood Dr (39.47440,-80.12290) - and '106 Overfort' matches nothing in the US Census address file or OpenStreetMap. Esri imagery at all three shows rural houses and mobile homes or dense city blocks, with no campground loop, pads or facilities. Where it is described at all it is 'full hookup RV sites catering to long term stays' with 'a few short term sites may be available - call first'. Dead everywhere plus thin, negative reviews = closed/defunct.

name: Wheeling Island Race Track & Gaming
skip_reason: Casino/racetrack overnight parking lot, not a campground - verified rather than skipped on the name. RV Life's 0 sites and avg_rate 0 both check out: Wheeling Island Hotel-Casino-Racetrack at 1 Stone St offers free RV parking on its paved lots (signage directs motorhomes to lot H, the far left lot) with no numbered sites, no hookups and no published nightly rate, and Allstays records the property's own rule that you may park an RV while gaming or staying in the hotel but may not stay in the RV. No separate campground exists on the island.
